answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to post a small copper-valued bond that is slashed if peers prove it misbehaves, while real work earns attestations over time. Like an ember that must be tended before it becomes a fire, a fresh identity starts with zero trust and cannot vote or claim rewards until established peers vouch for it. An atlas of these signed attestations makes fake identities expensive: creating a thousand clones costs a thousand bonds, yet buys no history.
